'''Ronald Joseph Radke''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|r|æ|d|k|i}}; born December 15, 1983) is an American singer, rapper, musician, and songwriter who is the frontman of rock band [[Falling in Reverse]] and former frontman of [[post-hardcore]] band [[Escape the Fate]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=An Honest Conversation With Ronnie Radke, Part 1: 'I'm Not Going To Shy Away From My Mis - Features|url=https://www.rocksound.tv/features/read/an-honest-conversation-with-ronnie-radke-part-1-im-not-going-to-shy-aw|access-date=2022-01-10|website=Rock Sound Magazine|language=en|archive-date=January 10, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220110034251/https://www.rocksound.tv/features/read/an-honest-conversation-with-ronnie-radke-part-1-im-not-going-to-shy-aw|url-status=dead}}</ref> He rose to popularity with Escape the Fate but was kicked out in 2008 after being sentenced to prison for violating probation. While in prison, Radke started a new band called From Behind These Walls, which later changed its name to Falling in Reverse. The band began recording upon his release from prison in December 2010.

As a solo musician, Radke released a [[Rapping|rap]] mixtape, ''Watch Me'', in 2014, which included collaborations with [[Deuce (musician)|Deuce]], {{notatypo|b.LaY}}, [[Tyler Carter]], [[Sy Ari da Kid]], [[Jacoby Shaddix]], [[Danny Worsnop]], [[Andy Biersack]], and [[Craig Mabbitt]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/falling-in-reverse-ronnie-radke-new-song-star-studded-mixtape/|title=Falling in Reverse's Ronnie Radke Offers Free Song Download From Star-Studded Mixtape|website=Loudwire|date=December 26, 2013 }}</ref>

Radke's vocal style incorporates [[rapping]], [[Screaming in music|screaming]] and [[Singing|clean vocals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Richardson |first=Jake RichardsonJake |date=2023-04-17 |title=10 Best Clean Singers in Metalcore |url=https://loudwire.com/best-clean-singers-metalcore/ |access-date=2025-12-22 |website=Loudwire |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==

Ronald Joseph Radke was born on December 15, 1983, in [[St. Rose Dominican Hospital – Rose de Lima Campus|St. Rose Hospital]], in [[Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], one of three children born to Russell Radke, the others being his brothers, Anthony James Radke (1980–2013) and Matthew Radke.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://musicjunkiepress.com/breaking-news/rest-in-peace-anthony-james-radke-older-brother-of-ronnie-radke/|title=Rest in Peace Anthony James Radke, older brother of Ronnie Radke - Music Junkie Press|date=August 11, 2013|newspaper=Music Junkie Press|language=en-US|access-date=January 16, 2017}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://peabodykansas.com/direct/anthony_radke+4447radke+416e74686f6e79205261646b65|title=Anthony Radke {{!}} Peabody Gazette-Bulletin {{!}} Aug. 15, 2013|website=peabodykansas.com|access-date=2018-10-25}}</ref> Radke's mother was a drug addict and was absent for much of his childhood. In a 2018 interview with ''Rock Sound'', he reflected that growing up without a mother figure led to difficulties in respecting women during his youth and early adulthood, and said that becoming a father helped him gain a new sense of respect and emotional maturity. He later forgave his mother and posted a picture of the two of them on Instagram after a Falling in Reverse show in 2014.<ref name="Rock Sound Magazine">{{Cite news|url=https://www.rocksound.tv/features/read/an-honest-conversation-with-ronnie-radke-part-2-im-not-this-egotistical-tyr|title=An Honest Conversation With Ronnie Radke, Part 2: I'm Not This Egotistical, Tyrannical Person' - Features - Rock Sound Magazine|work=Rock Sound Magazine|access-date=2018-10-25|language=en-GB|archive-date=July 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180716165924/https://www.rocksound.tv/features/read/an-honest-conversation-with-ronnie-radke-part-2-im-not-this-egotistical-tyr|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
===Escape the Fate (2004–2008)===
In high school, Radke and [[Max Green (musician)|Max Green]] were close friends. In 2004, Bryan Money, looking for a vocalist, contacted Max, who referred him to Radke. Bryan agreed and began auditions for a drummer. Robert Ortiz was selected, and [[Escape the Fate]] was formed. A few weeks later, [[Omar Espinosa]], who at the time was the guitarist for [[Lovehatehero]], joined as rhythm guitarist. The band began to play in the [[post-hardcore]] scene in Las Vegas. During that time [[Carson Allen]] joined as keyboardist. The band recorded the demo ''[[Escape the Fate (demo album)|Escape the Fate EP]]''. They signed in early 2006 with [[Epitaph Records]] after winning a radio contest judged by [[My Chemical Romance]], which launched their career.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/music/artist/escape_the_fate/artist.jhtml#biographyEnd|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080214184035/http://www.mtv.com/music/artist/escape_the_fate/artist.jhtml#biographyEnd|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 14, 2008|title=MTV Artist's, Escape the Fate Bio|publisher=MTV.com}}</ref>

In May 2006, recording for the EP ''[[There's No Sympathy for the Dead]]'' began, as well as some songs from the debut album, ''[[Dying Is Your Latest Fashion]]''. Both were produced by Radke's friend [[Michael "Elvis" Baskette]].

Radke was later kicked out of Escape the Fate in 2008 after he was sentenced to two and a half years in prison for violating a probation given to him for owning brass knuckles.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2014-01-22|title=When Falling in Reverse meets Escape the Fate, fans line up for their favorites - Las Vegas Weekly|url=https://lasvegasweekly.com/ae/music/2014/jan/22/when-falling-reverse-meets-escape-fate-fans-line-t/|access-date=2022-01-10|website=lasvegasweekly.com}}</ref> Radke had multiple previous brushes with the law due to prior narcotics offenses. He was replaced with former [[Blessthefall]] singer [[Craig Mabbitt]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Lofgren|first=Laura|title=Controversy: Escape the Fate's No. 1 Fan|url=http://www.kentwired.com/latest_updates/article_4d3f13e7-79d1-53dc-a5cc-3837b4b5550d.html|access-date=2022-01-10|website=KentWired.com|language=en|archive-date=January 10, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220110033917/http://www.kentwired.com/latest_updates/article_4d3f13e7-79d1-53dc-a5cc-3837b4b5550d.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

During Radke's incarceration, a feud grew between Radke and Mabbitt. Escape the Fate insulted Radke during live performances, and Radke responded with vulgar posts on social media. When Mabbitt began dating Radke's ex-girlfriend, who had starred in an earlier Escape the Fate music video, Radke asked Mabbitt, "How does my dick taste??" on [[Myspace]]. In response to a heckler during an Escape the Fate show at 2009's [[Warped Tour]], Mabbitt yelled, "You miss the old singer? He's locked up in Nevada. Go suck his fucking cock."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2014-01-09|title=Ronnie Radke vs. Escape The Fate: the scene's biggest feud and what we learned from it|url=https://www.altpress.com/features/ronnie_radke_vs-_escape_the_fate_the_scenes_biggest_feud_and_what_we_learne/|access-date=2022-01-10|website=Alternative Press Magazine|language=en}}</ref>

By October 28, 2013, Radke and Mabbit had made up and are now on good terms. Signifying an end to the hostilities, Escape the Fate and Falling in Reverse co-headlined the "Bury the Hatchet" tour in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Childers|first=Chad|title=Escape the Fate's Craig Mabbitt Talks 'Bury the Hatchet' Tour + Reconnecting With Ronnie Radke|url=https://loudwire.com/escape-the-fate-craig-mabbitt-bury-the-hatchet-tour-ronnie-radke/|access-date=2022-01-10|website=Loudwire|date=November 21, 2013 |language=en}}</ref>

===Falling in Reverse (2008–present)===
[[File:Falling in Reverse-Rock im Park 2014- by 2eight DSC9368.jpg|thumb|Radke with Falling in Reverse at [[Rock im Park]] 2014]]
While serving his sentence at [[High Desert State Prison (California)|High Desert State Prison]], Radke wrote the first material for his upcoming band, which he described as "[[Norma Jean (band)|Norma Jean]] or [[Underoath]] with [[Katy Perry]] choruses."<ref>{{Cite web|last=Zaleski|first=Annie|date=2011-05-05|title=Rocker Ronnie Radke is out of prison and ready to make his musical mark again - Las Vegas Sun Newspaper|url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2011/may/05/rocker-ronnie-radke-out-prison-and-ready-make-his-/#:~:text=In%20January%202008,%20he%20pled,probation%20and%20went%20to%20prison.|access-date=2022-01-10|website=lasvegassun.com|language=en}}</ref> With the help of Nason Schoeffler, Radke formed [[Falling in Reverse]], originally named From Behind these Walls.<ref name="Zaleski">{{cite web|last=Zaleski|first=Annie|date=December 22, 2010|title=Ex-Escape The Fate vocalist Ronnie Radke breaks his silence after prison release|url=http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/exclusive_ex-escape_the_fate_vocalist_ronnie_radke_breaks_his_silence_after/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110815193637/http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/exclusive_ex-escape_the_fate_vocalist_ronnie_radke_breaks_his_silence_after/|archive-date=August 15, 2011|access-date=January 28, 2013|publisher=Alternative Press}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Alternative Press Interview with Ronnie Radke|url=http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/exclusive_ex-escape_the_fate_vocalist_ronnie_radke_breaks_his_silence_after|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019223110/http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/exclusive_ex-escape_the_fate_vocalist_ronnie_radke_breaks_his_silence_after/|archive-date=October 19, 2013|access-date=May 13, 2011|publisher=Altpress.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.punknews.org/article/42949 |title=Ronnie Radke returns with Falling in Reverse |date=June 7, 2011 |publisher=Punknews.org |access-date=June 6, 2015}}</ref> Upon his release from prison in December 2010, Radke returned to recording. Falling In Reverse released their first single "Raised by Wolves" in 2010, followed by the album ''[[The Drug in Me Is You]]'' which was released on July 26, 2011, through [[Epitaph Records]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Drug in Me Is You Hits the selves|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=159159|publisher=Blabbermouth.net}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|year=2011|title=Onesheet announces The Drug in Me Is You premiere|url=http://onesheet.com/fallinginreverse/onesheet-biography/36831|publisher=Onesheet.com}}{{Dead link|date=August 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Falling in Reverse's first two albums reached the top 20 in the United States, and all four have charted in the top 40. The band's song "[[Popular Monster (song)|Popular Monster]]" became a No. 1 hit on ''Billboard''<nowiki/>'s [[Mainstream Rock (chart)|Mainstream Rock]] chart in 2020, their first chart-topper.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Childers|first=Chad|title=Falling in Reverse Hit Radio Milestone With 'Popular Monster'|url=https://loudwire.com/falling-in-reverse-no-1-popular-monster/|access-date=2022-01-11|website=Loudwire|date=April 29, 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

===Solo and ''Watch Me'' (2013–present)===
On May 31, 2013, Radke launched his YouTube channel and released a solo song, "Fair-Weather Fans". The song is described as "a song Ronnie made dedicated to all the people who didn't believe in him."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.altpress.com/news/entry/mysterious_ronnie_radke_track_surfaces_online|publisher=Alternative Press|first=Cassie|last=Whitt|title=Ronnie Radke launches YouTube channel, releases solo song "The Fairweather Fans"|date=May 31, 2013|access-date=June 1, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.killyourstereo.com/news/17555/ronnie-radke-posts-new-solo-song-fairweather-fans/|publisher=KillYourStereo.com|author=Simonk|title=Ronnie Radke post's new solo song 'Fairweather Fans'|date=June 1, 2013|access-date=June 2, 2013|archive-date=June 9, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609105340/http://www.killyourstereo.com/news/17555/ronnie-radke-posts-new-solo-song-fairweather-fans|url-status=dead}}</ref> On June 1, he released a second song, called "What Up Earth?".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.altpress.com/news/entry/ronnie_radke_posts_second_solo_song_what_up_earth|publisher=Alternative Press|first=Cassie|last=Whitt|title=Ronnie Radke posts second solo song, "What Up Earth?"|date=June 1, 2013|access-date=June 2, 2013}}</ref>

In part 3 of his interview with ''Alternative Press'', Radke stated that he is creating a rap mixtape, produced by Charles Massabo (Kallaghan Records)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://kallaghanrecords.com/blog/ |title=Kallaghan Records |publisher=Kallaghanrecords.com |access-date=June 6, 2015 |archive-date=May 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150506200253/http://kallaghanrecords.com/blog/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> that will feature some well known rap artists, the mixtape will be released in December 2013 for free.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/aptv_exclusive_a_conversation_with_ronnie_radke_part_three_changes_in_style|publisher=Alternative Press|first=Brandon|last=Waddell|title=Part 3|date=June 6, 2013|access-date=June 7, 2013}}</ref> The first single off that mixtape, "Blacklist", which features {{notatypo|b.LaY}}, was released on July 5, 2013, on YouTube.<ref>{{YouTube|4AJs24PIuWk|title=Ronnie Radke - Blacklist (feat. B.Lay) (Official Lyric Video)}}</ref>

A [[diss track]] titled "I Wash Cars" (also featuring {{notatypo|b.LaY}}), which attacks [[Sumerian Records]] and its founder [[Ash Avildsen]], [[Lorenzo Antonucci|Lorenzo "The Main Event" Antonucci]], and [[electronicore]] band [[I See Stars]], was leaked online. Ash and Lorenzo released a diss track in reply to "I Wash Cars" titled "When Ronnie Met Sally" attacking Radke. The feud between the two groups has since been resolved, and Radke is now on good terms with I See Stars, Sumerian Records, and Antonucci.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/ronnie_radke_sumerian_diss_tracks_full_lyrics |title=Ronnie Radke/Sumerian Diss Tracks Disappear: The Beef is Over, But We've Got Full Lyrics Right Here - Alternative Press |publisher=Altpress.com |access-date=June 6, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://altpress.com/news/entry/i_was_mad._its_not_how_i_feel_anymore_ronnie_radke_on_i_see_stars_dis_track |title=UPDATE: "It's not how I feel anymore" Ronnie Radke on I See Stars diss track; ISS call "truce" - Alternative Press |publisher=Altpress.com |access-date=June 6, 2015}}</ref>

In an interview with ''[[Loudwire]]'', he has stated that he is in the process of making a rap mixtape, which according to Radke would include an artist on every song. He has also stated that the mixtape may be released for around Christmas.<ref name="Ronnie Radke interview about Bury the Hatchet and Mix-tape">{{cite web|title=Falling in Reverse's Ronnie Radke Talks Upcoming Tour with Escape the Fate, Mix Tape + More|url=http://loudwire.com/falling-in-reverse-ronnie-radke-tour-escape-the-fate-mix-tape-more/|work=Loudwire|publisher=Chad Childers|access-date=November 24, 2013|format=Interview|date=November 20, 2013|quote=I'm giving it away for free to the fans. I just wanted to do something different in our scene that nobody's ever done...}}</ref> On Christmas Day, he revealed a website through which subscribers received a new song, "Destiny", from the mixtape, now titled ''Watch Me''. The track-list was also revealed but some songs did not contain feature other artists like he originally claimed. As of 2021, three songs from the mixtape have not seen official release.

In mid-2022, Radke made headlines from publications such as ''[[Loudwire]]'' when he and [[Papa Roach]] frontman [[Jacoby Shaddix]] slapped each other with tortillas while participating in the purported "Tortilla Slap Challenge".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-08-08 |title=Ronnie Radke + Jacoby Shaddix Slap Each Other in Tortilla Challenge |url=https://loudwire.com/ronnie-radke-jacoby-shaddix-tortilla-challenge-video/ |access-date=2025-12-19 |website=Loudwire |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Radke has one daughter from his relationship with model Crissy Henderson. At one point, he was engaged to Henderson, but their relationship ended in 2013 due to [[infidelity]] on his part.<ref name="Conversations with Radke">{{cite web |last=Downey |first=Ryan J. |date=June 4, 2013 |title=APTV Exclusive! A Conversation with Ronnie Radke part two: Fatherhood And Relationships |url=http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/aptv_exclusive_a_conversation_ronnie_radke_part_two_fatherhood_and_relation |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220314003415/https://www.altpress.com/features/aptv_exclusive_a_conversation_ronnie_radke_part_two_fatherhood_and_relation/ |archive-date=March 14, 2022 |access-date=June 8, 2013 |publisher=Alternative Press}}</ref>

Radke's older brother, Anthony, died from a [[traffic collision]] in 2013.<ref name=":0" />

In late 2018, Radke began a relationship with wrestler [[Saraya Bevis]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cosmopolitan.com/entertainment/celebs/a26252426/where-is-saraya-paige-bevis-now/|title=Where Is WWE Wrestler Saraya "Paige" Bevis Today?|website=Cosmopolitan|date=February 8, 2019|access-date=October 24, 2019}}</ref> They broke up in late 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tmz.com/2025/01/21/saraya-ronnie-radke-breakup/|title=AEW Star Saraya Splits From Ronnie Radke After 6 Years|date=January 21, 2025|website=TMZ}}</ref>

In December 2022, Radke released a memoir, ''I Can Explain'', written with journalist Ryan J. Downey. Radke said, "I named it that 'cause it's really funny to me 'cause I've gotten in so much trouble and have a bad reputation."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Childers |first=Chad |date=2022-08-31 |title=Falling in Reverse's Ronnie Radke Details PTSD From Prison Experience, Announces New Book |url=https://loudwire.com/falling-in-reverse-ronnie-radke-details-ptsd-prison-experience-i-can-explain-book/ |access-date=2023-08-03 |website=Loudwire |language=en}}</ref>

In December 2024, Radke was denied entry into the United Kingdom because of his prison sentence, forcing Falling in Reverse to cancel and postpone a scheduled UK tour.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Falling In Reverse UK tour cancelled as Ronnie Radke denied entry into the country |url=https://lambgoat.com/news/45073/falling-in-reverse-uk-tour-cancelled-as-ronnie-radke-denied-entry-into-the-country/ |access-date=2024-12-03 |website=lambgoat.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Legal issues==

=== Involvement in killing and prison sentence ===
On May 6, 2006, at approximately 2:30PM, Radke met with Marcel Colquitt in Las Vegas, Nevada at the north end of [[Decatur Boulevard]]  near [[Shadow Ridge High School (Nevada)|Shadow Ridge High School]] to fight.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McCabe |first=Francis |title=Two weekend homicide victims identified |date=2006-05-09 |work=Las Vegas Review-Journal |url=http://www.reviewjournal.com/lvrj_home/2006/May-09-Tue-2006/news/7298047.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060518121134/http://www.reviewjournal.com/lvrj_home/2006/May-09-Tue-2006/news/7298047.html |archive-date=2006-05-18}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://lasvegasweekly.com/news/archive/2008/feb/23/tragedy-murder-suicide-music-and-drugs/|title=[Tragedy] Murder, suicide, music and drugs|work=LasVegasWeekly.com|access-date=2018-10-18}}</ref> Each man brought additional men to support them in the fight. During the fight, 22-year-old Chase Rader, a man who had accompanied Radke, shot 18-year-old Michael Allen Cook, killing him, as well as wounding another man, Colquitt's brother.<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.lasvegasnow.com/news/iteam-no-charges-filed-in-2006-killing/82088377|title=I-Team: No Charges Filed in 2006 Killing|date=2008-03-11|work=LasVegasNow|access-date=2018-10-18|language=en-US}}{{Dead link|date=September 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Rader was arrested for and charged with murder but the [[district attorney]] declined to prosecute him, despite his [[confession]], as it was determined Rader acted in [[self-defense]].<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite news |last=Bryan |first=Beverly |date=2013-02-16 |title=Sour note |url=http://archives.lasvegascitylife.com/articles/2006/09/28/local_news/news03.txt#selection-487.0-487.846 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216082616/http://archives.lasvegascitylife.com/articles/2006/09/28/local_news/news03.txt#selection-487.0-487.846 |archive-date=2013-02-16 |access-date=2018-10-18 |work=[[Las Vegas CityLife]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Radke |first=Ronnie |date=January 21, 2022 |title=#greenscreen #LMFAO #shrek |url=https://www.tiktok.com/@ronnieradke/video/7055730280833010990?_r=1&_t=8XEBFQpWLmA |access-date=2023-02-11 |website=TikTok |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jericho |first=Talk Is |title=Talk Is Jericho - Falling Into Ronnie Radke |url=https://podcasts.google.com/feed/aHR0cHM6Ly9mZWVkcy5tZWdhcGhvbmUuZm0vV1dPOTc0MTAzMTQ4NQ/episode/ZWE5Y2MzMGQtNjZmNy00N2JlLWExNTktM2IxYmFmODRiN2U4 |access-date=2023-02-11 |website=Google Podcasts |language=en-US}}</ref>

Radke pleaded guilty to [[Battery (crime)|battery with substantial bodily harm]] and to owning and bringing brass knuckles to the brawl (illegal in Nevada); subsequently, he was placed on [[probation]] for five years and ordered to pay $92,372 in [[restitution]] to Ceda Freeman, Cook's mother.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="Sixthings">{{cite web|url=http://www.revolvermag.com/lists-2/falling-in-reverse-frontman-ronnie-radke-reveals-the-top-6-things-not-to-do-in-jail.html|title=Ronnie Radke Reveals Six Things Not To Do in Jail|first=Jon|last=Wiederhorn|date=September 28, 2011|publisher=Revolver|access-date=June 1, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=June 2012 |title=Ronnie Radke: Prison. Drugs. Death. Redemption. |work=Rock Sound Magazine}}</ref> After Radke violated the terms of his probation, he was sentenced to serve two and a half years in prison.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/falling-in-reverse-frontman-goes-from-jail-to-warped-main-stage-64753/|title=Falling in Reverse Frontman Goes from Jail to Warped Main Stage|last=Baltin|first=Steve|date=2012-04-05|magazine=Rolling Stone|access-date=2018-10-18|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://archives.lasvegascitylife.com/articles/2006/09/28/local_news/news03.txt|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216082616/http://archives.lasvegascitylife.com/articles/2006/09/28/local_news/news03.txt|url-status=dead|title=Las Vegas CityLife|date=February 16, 2013|archive-date=February 16, 2013}}</ref><ref name="auto1" />

Because of his prison sentence, [[Escape the Fate]] fired Radke. [[Craig Mabbitt]], formerly of the band [[Blessthefall]], replaced the imprisoned Radke.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/ronnie-radke-new-falling-in-reverse-bassist-trashes-former-band-escape-the-fate/|title=Ronnie Radke Announces New Falling in Reverse Bassist, Trashes Former Band Escape the Fate|website=Loudwire|date=January 19, 2012 |language=en|access-date=2018-10-18}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

=== Domestic violence arrest ===
On May 1, 2012, Radke was accused of striking his then-girlfriend, Sally Watts, and was subsequently arrested in [[Glendale, California]], on August 6, 2012, after he had failed to make an appearance at any of the scheduled [[court hearing]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whitt |first=Cassie|title=UPDATED: Ronnie Radke (Falling In Reverse) arrested on charges of alleged domestic assault |url=https://www.altpress.com/ronnie_radke_falling_in_reverse_arrested_on_charges_of_alleged_domestic_ass/ |access-date=2023-02-11 |website=Alternative Press Magazine |date=August 8, 2012 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Relationships">{{Cite web|url=https://liverampup.com/entertainment/ronnie-radke-s-ex-girlfriend-alerts-past-filled-drugs-being-arrested-dating-anyone-now.html|title=Ronnie Radke's Ex-Girlfriend Alerts About His Past Filled With Drugs And Being Arrested; Dating Anyone Now?|date=June 20, 2017|website=LIVERAMPUP}}</ref> He was officially charged with a [[misdemeanor]] count of corporal injury and misdemeanor false imprisonment by the [[Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/tn-gnp-0807-rock-singer-ronald-radke-arrested-in-glendale-on-domestic-assault-warrant-story.html|title=Rock singer arrested in Glendale on domestic assault warrant|last=jason.wells@latimes.com|first=Jason Wells|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=August 7, 2012 |access-date=2018-10-18}}</ref> He was released on $30,000 bail. On May 14, 2014, Radke pleaded [[no contest]] to [[disturbance of the peace]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Childers |first=Chad |title=Ronnie Radke Domestic Violence Charge Dropped |url=https://loudwire.com/ronnie-radke-domestic-violence-charge-dropped-new-song-deuce/ |access-date=2023-02-11 |website=Loudwire |date=May 16, 2014 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/ronnie_radke_was_in_court_today_for_domestic_violence/|title=Ronnie Radke in court today; domestic violence charge dismissed - Alternative Press|date=2014-05-14|work=Alternative Press|access-date=2018-10-18|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Six Flags assault arrest ===
On September 29, 2012, Radke was performing as part of [[Falling in Reverse]] for FestEVIL, a [[heavy metal music|metal]] festival for [[Six Flags Great Adventure]]'s [[Six Flags Fright Fest|Fright Fest]] event, when he threw three microphone stands into the audience at the close of a performance, injuring a 16-year-old girl, who was taken to the hospital, and a 24-year-old man, who was treated at the scene.<ref>{{cite web|first=Sammi |last=Chichester |url=http://www.revolvermag.com/news/falling-in-reverse-singer-ronnie-radke-arrested-2.html |title=Falling in Reverse Singer Ronnie Radke Arrested for Injuring Two Fans, But He Did Pay The Girl's Hospital Bill |work=Revolvermag |publisher=Revolvermag.com |date=October 3, 2012 |access-date=January 28, 2013}}</ref> Radke was charged with simple assault and aggravated assault and released on $25,000 bail.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nbcmiami.com/entertainment/music/Singer-Arrested-After-Throwing-Mic-Stands-Into-Crowd--172285881.html|title=Rocker's Mic Toss Leads to NJ Arrest|work=NBC 6 South Florida|access-date=2018-10-18|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailyrecord.com/article/20121001/NJNEWS10/310010050/Singer-Ronnie-Radke-Falling-Reverse-accused-throwing-microphone-stands-Great-Adventure?nclick_check=1|title=Singer Ronnie Radke of Falling in Reverse accused of throwing microphone stands at Great Adventure|date=October 1, 2012|publisher=Dailyrecord.com|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130215191443/http://www.dailyrecord.com/article/20121001/NJNEWS10/310010050/Singer-Ronnie-Radke-Falling-Reverse-accused-throwing-microphone-stands-Great-Adventure?nclick_check=1|archive-date=February 15, 2013|url-status=dead|access-date=January 28, 2013}}</ref> Radke publicly apologized for his actions, saying that his actions were not in anger and that he had not intended to hurt anyone.<ref>{{Cite web |last=|first=|title=APTV Exclusive! A Conversation With Ronnie Radke part three: Changes In Style|url=https://www.altpress.com/aptv_exclusive_a_conversation_with_ronnie_radke_part_three_changes_in_style/|access-date=2023-02-11|website=Alternative Press Magazine|date=June 6, 2013|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230211183934/https://www.altpress.com/aptv_exclusive_a_conversation_with_ronnie_radke_part_three_changes_in_style/|archive-date=February 11, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Rock Sound Magazine" /> [[Six Flags]] subsequently decided to ban hard rock and heavy metal bands from performing at the park in the future.<ref>{{cite web|first=Michele |last=Angermiller |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/earshot/six-flags-great-adventure-ban-metal-concerts-376033 |title=Six Flags Great Adventure Bans Metal Concerts Following Microphone Stand Throwing Incident |website=Hollywoodreporter.com |date=October 3, 2012 |access-date=January 28, 2013}}</ref>

In the years following, he has since claimed that he never apologized for the incident and does not plan to because it "helped [his] persona", stating "I'll fucking do it again."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ronnie Radke Claims Woman Received "Almost a Million Dollars" for Getting Hit With Mic Stand in 2012|url=https://notetoscene.com/ronnie-radke-woman-million-dollars-mic-stand/|website=Note To Scene|date=2020-01-16|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Radke |first=Ronnie |date=August 7, 2025 |title=I Lost My Lawsuit with Anthony Fantano |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mfAcZro95ms |access-date=October 5, 2025 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

=== Rape allegation and defamation lawsuit ===
On June 10, 2015, it was reported that Radke had been publicly accused of sexual assault by a 25-year-old woman. The accuser alleged that Radke had sexually assaulted her after Falling in Reverse's performance at the [[Murray Theater (Murray, Utah)|Murray Theater]] on June 3, 2015. Though it was determined that Radke had contact with the woman, police found no evidence that Radke or his entourage had assaulted the woman.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/ronnie_radke_sues_accuser_for_defamation/|title=Ronnie Radke Sues Accuser for Defamation - Alternative Press|date=2015-06-08|work=Alternative Press|access-date=2018-10-18|language=en-US}}</ref> Radke subsequently filed a lawsuit for [[defamation]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.altpress.com/features/ronnie_radkes_accuser_speaks_exclusive/|title=Ronnie Radke's Accuser Speaks (Exclusive) - Alternative Press|date=2015-06-10|work=Alternative Press|access-date=2018-10-18|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Falling In Reverse's Ronnie Radke Sues Sexual Assault Accuser |url=https://loudwire.com/falling-in-reverse-ronnie-radke-sues-sexual-assault-accuser/ |access-date=2023-02-11 |website=Loudwire |date= June 9, 2015|language=en}}</ref>

=== Anthony Fantano defamation lawsuit ===
In August 2024, Radke filed a [[defamation lawsuit]] against online music critic [[Anthony Fantano]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Childers |first=Chad |date=2024-08-22 |title=Report – Falling in Reverse's Ronnie Radke Files Defamation Suit Against Critic Anthony Fantano |url=https://loudwire.com/falling-in-reverse-ronnie-radke-defamation-suit-against-anthony-fantano/ |access-date=2024-08-22 |website=Loudwire |language=en}}</ref> In the lawsuit, Radke accused Fantano of defaming him in a video titled "This Guy Sucks", as well as a since-deleted tweet where [[Monuments (metal band)|Monuments']] frontman [[Andy Cizek]] referred to Radke as the "[[Bill Cosby]] of alt music".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Chelosky|first=Danielle|date=2024-08-22 |title=Falling In Reverse Frontman Ronnie Radke Sues Anthony Fantano For Defamation |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2277321/falling-in-reverse-frontman-ronnie-radke-sues-anthony-fantano-for-defamation/news/ |access-date=2024-12-03 |website=Stereogum |language=en}}</ref> The case was later dismissed under the [[anti-SLAPP]] statute in Fantano's favor with Radke ordered to pay Fantano's legal fees.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/the-needle-drops-anthony-fantano-speaks-out-after-winning-defamation-suit-against-falling-in-reverses-ronnie-radke-3888656|title=The Needle Drop's Anthony Fantano speaks out after winning defamation suit against Falling In Reverse's Ronnie Radke|date=2025-08-25|accessdate=2025-09-24|first=Max|last=Pilley|publisher=[[NME]]}}</ref>
